target_customer: PC gamers with laptops too weak for modern games, and owners of idle GPUs such as crypto mining rigs
problem: High end PC gaming needs expensive hardware. Vectordash streamed games from rented, privately owned GPUs to ordinary laptops.
business_model: Subscription of $28 per month for gamers, with payouts of $60 to $105 per month to GPU hosts (per TechCrunch)

founders.name: Abhishek Bhargava
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder with no background.

founders.name: Sharif Shameem
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch (2019-03-16), not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Parsec
competitors.what: Game streaming software that lets people stream a powerful PC, including rented cloud machines, to another device
competitors.traction_then: Operating on AWS per a 2018 article

competitors.name: Shadow
competitors.what: Subscription cloud PC with its own data centers
competitors.traction_then: Own data center infrastructure per Fortune

competitors.name: Nvidia GeForce Now
competitors.what: Cloud gaming service run by Nvidia

technical_complexity.rationale: Low latency streaming of 4K 60 FPS across consumer GPUs hosted at home, with matching by distance within about 300 miles.

defensibility.rationale: TechCrunch notes a large provider could undercut on price; no exclusive hardware or contracts and the supply side was commodity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google announced Stadia in March 2019 and a third party blog framed it as a death blow to Vectordash, though I could not read that article.

market_need_then: Interest in cloud gaming was high in 2018 and 2019 with Stadia and GeForce Now, and crypto miners had idle GPUs after the 2018 price crash per TechCrunch's framing.

branding.domain_note: Used vectordash.com, exact .com. The domain did not resolve when fetched in 2026-11.
branding.community_and_virality: Launch coverage by TechCrunch, Tom's Hardware, HotHardware and TechSpot; a founder tweet showing Apex Legends on a 13 inch Mac circulated

brand_strength.rationale: Good launch press in March 2019 but a generic technical name and no continuing community evidence.

outcome_analysis: Vectordash launched out of YC Winter 2019 with press coverage in March 2019 for a peer hosted cloud gaming service, just as Google Stadia and Nvidia GeForce Now were scaling. The model of paying hosts 60 to 105 dollars while charging gamers 28 dollars looked hard on unit economics, which TechCrunch raised, and well funded platforms could undercut it. The YC directory lists it inactive but no shutdown cause was found; the failure factors are inferred from the launch coverage and are low confidence.
notes: The $150K seed rests on CB Insights alone. MarketScreener snippets named Arbaz Khatib as another founder and give Bhargava a CTO title 2017 to 2021; not opened so not recorded. Competitor details come from a search summary of the Fortune 2018 article that I did not open directly; Shadow, Parsec and GeForce Now claims were taken from that summary. The Stadia 'death blow' article could not be read. Website did not resolve.
